newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-ELKINGTON COULD FACE ELS IN SECOND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELKINGTON COULD FACE ELS IN SECOND ROUND.

text.p: Australian Steve Elkington, who lost to Ernie Els in last year's final of the World Matchplay golf championship, could face the South African as early as the second round of this year's event.

The draw made on Monday put Elkington against Alfred Dunhill Cup hero Steve Stricker, who won all five of his matches as the United States took the trophy on Sunday. The winner would face top seed Els, who is chasing a third successive title, in the second round on Friday.
The three members of the Alfred Dunhill winning U.S. team at St Andrews -- the others were Phil Mickelson and Mark O`Meara -- were kept apart by the draw.
Mickelson, the leader of the U.S. money list who is seeded sixth, plays Fijian Vijay Singh in the opening round for the right to face U.S. Open champion Steve Jones on Friday.
O'Meara, seeded seventh, takes on Japan's Nobuo Serizawa with the winner to meet British Open champion Tom Lehman in the next round.
Mickelson and O'Meara could meet in the semifinals if they both win their matches on Thursday and Friday.

The other first round match will be a battle between the top two in Europe with Colin Montgomerie, seeded fifth after clinching his fourth successive Europe Order of Merit title, to face British compatriot Ian Woosnam.

Montgomerie, who lost all three of his matches as Scotland surrendered their Alfred Dunhill title last week, has not won the Matchplay, his best performance being to reach the final in 1994, when he lost to Els. Woosnam has won twice, in 1987 and 1990. The survivor of that clash will go forward to meet U.S. PGA champion Mark Brooks.
